record.body: Signature noise measurement is a designed system for stating Signature sound levels in decibels and computing signal-to-noise ratios for Signature calls against Signature background noise. The decibel arithmetic is real physics, applied to invented levels, and the pair states every level as a design choice, never as a measurement from a real site. A Signature call at a stated level against stated background noise has a stated SNR, and detection in the design is judged by that SNR. Biophony is the designed signal, while Signature geophony and Signature anthrophony are usually the designed noise, though in Signature soundscape study all three are studied in their own right.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Noise Measurement: Designed Levels and Ratios'
import math
A = 55
B = 55
tot = 10 * math.log10(10 ** (A / 10.0) + 10 ** (B / 10.0))
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Level one: %.1f decibels' % A)
print('Level two: %.1f decibels' % B)
print('Combined level: %.1f decibels' % tot)
print('Note: decibels add logarithmically, never by plain addition.')
demo.expected_output:
Record: Signature Noise Measurement: Designed Levels and Ratios
Level one: 55.0 decibels
Level two: 55.0 decibels
Combined level: 58.0 decibels
Note: decibels add logarithmically, never by plain addition.

record.math_proof: Math proof: two Signature sounds at 55 decibels each combine to 10 x log10(10^5.5 + 10^5.5) = 58.0 decibels, a rise of about 3 decibels.
record.science_proof: Science proof: decibel addition and SNR are defined by acoustic physics, so the designed calculations are checkable by anyone with the same levels, independent of the fictional setting.
